title: Cumulative capstone: audit a carbon-conversion proposal
promptMarkdown:
Write a coherent 1200–1800-word report (equations/tables excluded; a comparably complete annotated calculation is acceptable) on this stipulated educational model, not a claim about a real device. At298.15K a cell reduces CO₂+2H⁺+2e⁻→HCOOH. Take its illustrative E°red=−0.200V, a(CO₂)=1.00, a(HCOOH)=0.0100 and pH2.00. The other half cell has reduction potential+0.100V under its maintained conditions and is used as the anode. A supply operates at1.50V,0.500A for60.0min with product Faradaic efficiency0.800. Use R=8.31446Jmol⁻¹K⁻¹, F=96485Cmol⁻¹, M(HCOOH)=46.025gmol⁻¹, pKa(HCOOH)=3.75; activities are ideal approximations. A candidate catalyst has a group-10 M²⁺ centre with four neutral monodentate donors and is diamagnetic. A manager claims “the catalyst changes K, heating always raises equilibrium yield, and current proves carbon conversion.”

(a) Balance atoms/charge and carbon oxidation states; describe Lewis/VSEPR CO₂ shape and polarity. (b) Derive Q and Ered, Ecell, and ΔrG per mole of the cell reaction; state the minimum reversible electrical energy needed for forward conversion under these conditions and why a real supply may exceed it. (c) At the stated pH calculate the formate/neutral-acid ratio; distinguish free neutral product from total product and explain the limitations of holding all supplied activities fixed during the full run. (d) Calculate charge, neutral-acid-equivalent product amount/mass, supplied energy and energy per mole of intended product. (e) Infer d count and compare plausible square-planar/tetrahedral models with limits. (f) Correct each managerial claim and design a controlled measurement plan covering product identification/amount, catalyst activity, mass/charge consistency and an equilibrium-versus-rate comparison. Include one consistency check and one unresolved real-device limitation.
hintLadder: Begin with a species/charge table and identify which potential is a reduction potential.
Keep Ecell=Ecathode,red−Eanode,red even for an externally driven unfavourable forward reaction.
Use pH and pKa to distinguish neutral acid from acid equivalents; current efficiency concerns total formed equivalents.
Track charge, useful product amount and supply energy separately, then test each managerial claim with a discriminating measurement.
